sections.h2: Choosing how to sell in West Melbourne
sections.html:
Owners in West Melbourne have three realistic options: a standard agent listing, a cash purchase, or an investor who wants the house with no repairs. Speed and price pull in opposite directions on each. What you pick depends on how the roof and major systems look, how soon you need funds, and any debt attached to the title.

  • Agent listing: usually the highest sale price, but showings, repairs and waiting on a buyer's mortgage add weeks.
  • Cash buyer or investor: fewer contingencies and timing you can often pick, though the price tends to run lower.
  • Sale after a repair push: worth it only when the work is cosmetic and cheap, because permits and inspections take time.

No matter who buys, write the terms down and decide who covers the deed tax, title search and recording. Those costs are negotiable in Florida, so put the answer in the contract instead of leaving it to a handshake.

sections.h2: West Melbourne homes and what inspectors look at
sections.html:
West Melbourne is in Brevard County, and the city grew quickly after it was created in 1959, from 3,050 people in 1970 to 25,924 in 2020. A lot of the housing stock was built during those fast-growth decades, which is why inspectors tend to focus on roofs, air conditioning and electrical work. Cash buyers usually reduce their offer for such items instead of asking you to repair them.

Water comes from the City of Melbourne and reaches customers through lines and meters the city owns, while a private contractor runs the wastewater plant. If your home is on city sewer, the closing agent will want a final utility reading and a clear account. A property on a septic tank is a different case, so tell any buyer early which system serves the house.

Sewer tie-in inspections are scheduled Monday through Thursday only. If an earlier owner hooked up to sewer, request the permit record from the Building Department. It shows buyers the connection passed inspection.

Work done without a permit tends to come up once a buyer's inspector or lender starts asking. Starting a project that needs a permit without one can bring code enforcement proceedings.

A recent Florida change, House Bill 803, allows certain permit exemptions for small home improvement projects under $7,500 on single family homes, duplexes and townhomes outside flood zones. Electrical, plumbing, structural work (including exterior doors, windows, roofing and sheds), mechanical and gas work still need a permit regardless of cost. You have to request an exemption in writing before the work starts.

sections.h2: Can a buyer rent out a West Melbourne house?
sections.html:
Yes, but the city expects a business tax receipt for rentals. A separate rental application is linked from the city's Business Tax Receipts page, and a business must hold a receipt showing the owner has registered and paid local tax.

Penalties apply unless renewal payments arrive by September 30. New owners must submit a fresh application with the deed or a bill of sale, and a buyer of a house with tenants should plan on that. The Finance Department answers questions at 321-327-6614 or 321-327-6616.

Landlords should hand the buyer the current rental receipt and let the tenant know about the sale. If either side wants the house empty at closing, put that in the contract.

One Brevard County bill carries every levy on a West Melbourne parcel. The Property Appraiser decides value. The county commissioners, school board, city and other bodies set millage, where one mill means one dollar for every thousand dollars of value. The Tax Collector's office number is (321) 264-6969.

The bill is mailed to the last address on record, and lenders who escrow usually ask for it directly. If nothing arrives, you still owe the tax and should request the amount before it goes delinquent.

  • Assessments are set as of January 1, and homestead requires the house to be your permanent residence by that date.
  • The exemption lasts only while you live there and do not rent it out.
  • For the next owner, value resets to just value the following January 1, so your tax figure will not simply carry over.

Delinquency starts April 1. Because bills come after the year ends, the closing agent prorates that year's tax between you and the buyer, and you should see the split in writing.

sections.h2: Closing costs on a West Melbourne deed
sections.html:
Deeds in Florida carry a documentary stamp tax of $0.70 per $100 of price. Whoever the contract says will pay, all parties to the document remain liable, and the clerk takes the money at recording.

Under Section 28.24, recording runs $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each one after it, with a $1.00 and 50 cent trust fund charge and a $4 per page technology charge. The itemized statement from the closing agent shows the actual total.

A cash offer does not erase these costs. It changes who negotiates them, so compare offers by net proceeds on the final statement and not by the headline number.

sections.h2: What if you owe taxes or the title is cloudy?
sections.html:
Back taxes create a lien problem but not a dead end. A title company finds any tax certificate or lien on the house and pays it from your proceeds at closing, so you can still sell.

Disclose known problems to buyers early. An investor can often work around a title issue or an unpermitted addition, but a surprise found late can kill the deal or lower the price.

Most quick sales follow one pattern. First you gather your deed, a payoff figure and recent tax bills, then accept an offer. The buyer may inspect, and a title company looks for liens and open permits. A settlement statement lists each charge. After you sign, the clerk records the deed and you receive what is left once payoffs and taxes are covered.

Cash buyers skip the lender's appraisal, the point where financed deals usually slow down. Ask about the closing date and deposit up front, and whether closing can happen before the next tax bill arrives.

faqs.q: Can I sell my West Melbourne house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. Inspections can bring repair requests from a lender or retail buyer, while a cash buyer taking it as-is typically folds condition into the price. Ask the Building Department about any open permits first.

faqs.q: Is there a local transfer tax in West Melbourne?
faqs.a: The state deed tax is $0.70 for each $100 of price, taken by the clerk at recording. Look over the draft settlement statement for any other charge.

faqs.q: Are permits needed for minor fixes made before listing?
faqs.a: Often. House Bill 803 can exempt a few small jobs under $7,500 on single family homes outside flood zones. Electrical, plumbing, roofing and other structural work still need permits, and any exemption must be requested in writing first.

faqs.q: What happens to my rental receipt when I sell?
faqs.a: Your buyer applies for a new business tax receipt and attaches the deed or a bill of sale. The city Finance Department, at 321-327-6614, can walk you through it.

faqs.q: When are Brevard County property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1, with certificates sold by June 1. At closing, the year of sale's bill is split between buyer and seller.
